lens: STORY & CURIOSITY (promo): hook in the first seconds, rhythm over ~90 s, one idea per beat, payoff, a clear end card and call to action; would a buyer want to try it?
method: The qa/sheets contact sheets for 14 of 15 shots are dated 17:10, which is before the round-1 review and the 82.71 s re-clock. QA flags this as coverage: 'older than the timeline'. So I judged from frames pulled from render/film.mp4 (rendered 22:17Z): 2 fps across the whole film, plus close stills at 3.9, 4.3, 30.2, 54.6-56.2 (5 fps), 56.9, 62.8-67.0, 65.2, 69.6, 72.6 and 80.0 s, checked against the word times in narration/timeline.json.
ledgerCheck: film.json stages.fixes is EMPTY. There is no round1-global and no round1-shots ledger, so no id is marked fixed, partial or skipped. Against the round-1 verdict, the render shows these director changes done: ch04-s01 and ch04-s02 redrawn with no owner URL, ch05-s05 cut with the agent pair moved into ch06-s01, the end-card hold extended, and the L0601 masking fixed. These routed shot fixes are NOT in the render: ch01-s01 (no early hook seed), ch02-s01 (URL still types leftward from the right edge), ch03-s01 (no explore footage), ch04-s03 (braces still on the 'Environment' header), ch05-s02 (no zoom), ch05-s04 (still static under L0508), ch06-s02 (no hook line, and the chip is still there). ch05-s03 is only partly fixed: the re-light exists but lands before 'time-travel'.
summary: The film is better where the director worked on it. The always-on run is now clean and confident: a drawn 3:00 AM with run cards turning green under a moon, then one URL bar that morphs staging → preview → localhost while pills light. The agent beat now sits quietly and readably under the triad: 'not yet' lands on 'recording' and 'good' lands on 'confirm'. That is the subtle touch the brief asked for. The story problems from round 1 are almost all still there, because the routed shot fixes were never run (empty ledger, stale sheets). The hook still sells only convenience. The USP visual ('A time-travel recording can') fires at 55.6-55.9 s, before the word, and cuts to the root-cause card just as 'time-travel' starts (56.44 s), so the differentiator is still told rather than shown. 'It kept starting over' runs over 4 s of identical frames. The end card never prints the closing promise and still has no call to action. A buyer comes away with 'managed, scheduled, records everything' but not a felt reason to try it today.

issues.problem: The USP payoff is mistimed. Rendered frames show the 27-square ghost grid re-lighting at 55.6-55.9 s, on 'that' (55.58), and then a match cut to the ROOT CAUSE card at about 56.0 s. So the whole of 'A time-travel recording can' (56.29-57.47 s) plays over the root-cause card, and the re-light lasts about 0.3 s. There is no rewind playhead sweep and no 'all 27 renders' label in any frame. The root-cause crop is unchanged, still opening on literal backticks ('`SidebarProjectList` trees { are not memoized }'). Round 1 marked this subject as misattributed.
issues.fix: Anchor the re-light to T.word('L0506','time-travel') (56.44 s). Hold the screen-recording frame with its 2 squares from 'screen' (54.43) to 'that' (55.58). On 'time-travel', sweep the kit rewind playhead right to left across the grid while all 27 squares re-light, and add our label 'all 27 renders'. Hold through 'recording' (57.03), then cut to ROOT CAUSE on 'can' (57.47); extend holdAfter so '{ root cause }' reads at least 1.5 s. Re-crop the clause so its real subject is intact and it does not start on a backtick. Verify on render frames at 55.4, 56.5, 57.0, 57.6 and 58.2 s.

issues.problem: Not fixed since round 1. From 62.8 s to 67.0 s (all of L0508, 'It never saved its place, so it kept starting over') the frames are identical: '258', the bars, a tiny 'checkpoint -1' flag that never moves forward and the struck cursor. The explanation half of the film's most memorable bug has no motion. There is no 'illustration' tag on the bars, and the struck-through cursor still sits next to '≈ 160 s · 2 clicks', which contradicts itself.
issues.fix: Do the round-1 note. Use a flag of at least 28 px that makes three forward tries of at least 80 px, each snapping back to 'checkpoint -1', on 'never' (63.40), 'place' (64.03) and 'kept' (65.32). On 'starting' (65.56), snap the counter 258 → 0 and race it back to 258 in about 0.5 s while the bars redraw from the left. Add a grey 'illustration' tag under the bars. Replace the struck cursor with a struck keyboard glyph that matches 'no keypresses'. Verify at 63.5, 64.1, 65.6, 65.9 and 66.5 s.

issues.problem: The end card is unchanged in substance. Frames at 76-82.7 s show '{ End-to-end testing · fully managed }', the Replay QA mark with the black '▶ recording' chip still glued beside it, and 'qa.replay.io' typed at about 28 px. 'Catch bugs that only exist in time' (77.54-79.08 s), the film's own hook, never appears on screen. There is no verb or next step, so the card reads as a brand plate, not an invitation.
issues.fix: On 'Catch' (77.54), grow a second line under the bracket line: 'Catch bugs that only exist { in time }', with the braces parting as in ch05-s01. After 'time' (79.08), type qa.replay.io into the same typed-prompt field, caret and all, that opened ch02-s01, with an eyebrow above it such as 'Point it at your app' or 'Try it free'. Use wording the product page really uses; check capture/api or research for the real CTA. Fade out the '▶ recording' chip before the URL types. Verify at 77.8, 79.3, 80.5 and 82.4 s.

issues.problem: The hook still sells convenience only. Frames at 3.9 and 4.3 s show the full line and then the blur, and the hold after 'run' (3.35 s) has no frame ribbon and no rewind playhead. Nothing in the first 13 s hints that this product sees what other test tools cannot, and the differentiator still first appears at 36.4 s (44 % in). The 'remember to run.' sweep also ends in pale peach-orange on peach haze, with low contrast at 3.9 s.
issues.fix: In the hold after 'run' (about 3.6-4.4 s), turn one drifting hairline into a faint frame ribbon with the red-pink rewind playhead running backwards across it for about 0.6 s. This is the same object ch05-s01 pays off, so the turn is planted. End the grad sweep at a deeper orange (about #f06a3c) or add a soft shadow. Verify at 3.7, 4.0 and 4.3 s.

issues.problem: Not fixed since round 1. At 30.2 s ('pull request'), empty braces with corner dots frame the 'Environment' column header, and a red mark strikes through its first letter. The PR #3 badges sit about 45 px lower, unmarked. The crop still slices the tab bar ('est Runs', 'Playwri' cut by the edges). The 'every pull request' moment points at nothing.
issues.fix: Anchor the braces and underline on the first purple 'PR #3' badge, measured on the RENDERED frame rather than a harness probe. Tighten the crop so it starts at the full 'Test Runs' heading, with no clipped tab text on either edge. Verify on render frames at 29.6, 30.2 and 30.8 s.

issues.problem: Not fixed since round 1. For 6.8 s (13.9-20.7 s), the step list sits in the left third, and the right two-thirds of the frame are empty paper while the narrator says 'It explores your app in a real browser'. The film's only proof of 'fully managed', 'Insights: 89 explorations · 1151 journeys', is still a grey footnote of about 12 px.
issues.fix: Float the explore take (MARKS.explore) as an RrwebScreen on the right two-thirds, cropped to the exploration player, with no owner sidebar, URL or login line. Tick 'Explore' as it plays. On 'journeys' (L0302), lift '1151 journeys' off the Insights line as a legible kit pill. Verify on render frames at 15.0, 17.5 and 19.5 s.

issues.problem: Partly fixed. The frame ribbon and the 'illustration · 16.7 ms frame budget' label are now on the plate, and the four hollow frames light. But there is still no zoom: the 67 ms block and the ribbon fill a thin band of a large black plate for all 11.3 s, the longest shot in the film. The jargon title dominates the top third. From 46.0 s the struck cursor floats outside the card on the plum background, detached from the plate. No 'background refresh' tag is visible.
issues.fix: On 'Sixty-seven' (b-ms67), zoom 1.0 → 1.5 onto the ribbon so the 67 ms bar and the four dropped frames fill the middle, and ease back on 'No click'. Put the struck cursor inside the plate, next to the ribbon. On 'background', ride a small tag 'background refresh · no user action' into the ribbon. Verify on render frames at 43.5, 45.5, 47.5 and 49.5 s.

issues.problem: The round-1 shot fixes were never run, or never closed. film.json stages.fixes is empty, there is no round1-shots ledger, and 14 of the 15 contact sheets in qa/sheets predate the review. QA warns 'coverage: older than the timeline' for 10 shots and 'cards/ghostText: changed since the audit' for 5. Seven routed shots are unchanged in the render. Reviewers cannot confirm any fix against a ledger.
issues.fix: Run film-shots on the routed ids (ch01-s01, ch02-s01, ch03-s01, ch04-s03, ch05-s02, ch05-s03, ch05-s04, ch06-s02 and ch06-s01) with ledger 'round2-shots', and close it with generator/film/shot-ledger.mjs finalize. Write 'round2-global' for the director's changes (ch04-s01/02 redraw, ch05-s05 cut, re-clock). Then re-assemble with a full re-sheet (film-assemble --all) so the next review has current sheets.

issues.problem: The agent beat works and stays secondary: 'not yet' lands about 69.6 s and 'good' about 72.6 s, on 'confirm'. But the travelling '▶ recording' chip slides over the triad's own words, hiding 'a r' of 'a root cause' at about 72.0 s and sitting on it at 72.6 s. At 69.6 s the passed chip covers the critic card's name. The 'developer' and 'critic' labels are about 10 px at 1080p, below the 22 px floor.
issues.fix: Route the chips along the rail between the two agent cards and below row 3 only, never over a word or a card label. Raise the card names to at least 22 px while keeping scale near 0.5. Verify at 69.6, 72.0 and 72.6 s.

issues.problem: Not fixed. At about 8.2-8.7 s the URL types leftward from the right frame edge ('https://|' hugging the edge, 'https://staging.your-app.dev' finishing flush right), with a blurred ghost line at the left. The film's first product beat looks off-balance.
issues.fix: Anchor the text at its final centred left x so it types left to right with at least 120 px of safe margin. Remove the ghost line or make it the recognisable blurred New-project page. Verify at 8.2, 8.7 and 9.6 s.

issues.problem: L0601 masking is fixed, but QA lineMasking still warns on L0402 (8.5 dB) and L0403 (9.6 dB): 'Against staging, a preview, even localhost' and 'And on every pull request', which are two of the three always-on claims a buyer needs to hear.
issues.fix: Thin the pluck and open-hat layer under 25.8-28.5 s and 29.2-31.0 s (or high-pass it toward 4-6 kHz while he speaks) to reach at least 10 dB line-over-music, and keep the stabs on transients.

issues.problem: The shelf copy is stale, which is why the latest critic score is missing from the UI. generator/film/publish.mjs writes public/generated/<slug>/review.json (the score shown under the player) from the newest qa/reviews/round-<n>/verdict.json, but publish last ran at 21:11:16Z. That is 7 minutes BEFORE round-1's verdict (21:18:35Z), so public/generated/replay-qa-promo/ has no review.json. QA 'current' also warns that the shelf runtime is 84.25 s while the timeline is 82.71 s.
issues.fix: Re-run film:publish for replay-qa-promo after this round's verdict is written. In film-review (or film-loop), call publish (or just the latestReview → review.json step) whenever a new verdict.json lands, so the UI always shows the newest round.

issues.problem: The rhythm in 13.9-36.4 s is still dense: 5 lines at 195-199 wpm (L0202, L0301, L0302, L0401, L0508) and about 11 capabilities in 22 s. 'and what's slow', which sets up the turn, gets only about 0.8 s before the tape-stop.
issues.fix: After the shot fixes, spend some of the 7 s of headroom under the 90 s target: add about 0.3 s of holdAfter on ch03-s01 and ch04-s02 and about 0.4 s on ch04-s03, then re-fit m01 to the new clock.

best_moments: ch04-s01 (20.7-25.5 s): the redrawn '3:00 AM' with five run cards filling, a moon rising and the cards turning green over 'Sep 1 … every Tuesday … Oct 6' ticks. 'While you sleep' finally has a picture, and it is clean.
ch04-s02 (25.5-29.0 s): one URL bar morphing staging → pr-42.preview → localhost:3000 while '{ staging · preview · local }' pills light one by one. One idea, one gesture, perfectly paced.

ch06-s01 (67-74 s): the developer and critic cards sit small and quiet under 'every run / a recording · every bug / a root cause · every fix / rerun to confirm', and 'not yet' turns to 'good' exactly on 'confirm'. The brief's subtle beat, done right.
ch05-s01 (36.4-39.2 s): the tape-stop into plum, the frame ribbon with a backwards playhead, and '{ in time }' landing as it stops. Still the film's turn.
ch05-s04: the request counter racing to 258 and stopping dead under the real bug title, the most memorable number in the film.
ch05-s03: the 67 ms block shattering into the 9 × 3 grid, '25 of 27 renders changed nothing'. An honest picture of an invisible bug.
